images.title: Place values of 27.53
images.purpose: Show that each digit of a decimal has a place value: tens, ones, tenths and hundredths.
images.composition: One place value chart sits in the centre of the frame with the number 27.53 written large above it; generous white space on all sides.
exact_structure: Above the chart, the number "27.53" written large and centred, with its 5 in teal #0072B2 and its 3 in amber #E69F00, and 2 and 7 in dark text #1F2937.
Below it, one place value chart of 4 columns and 2 rows with a #2B2B2B outline: a header row and one digit row.
Header row, left to right: "Tens", "Ones", "Tenths", "Hundredths"; the Tenths header cell has a light teal #0072B2 fill and the Hundredths header cell a light amber #E69F00 fill.

Between the Ones column and the Tenths column, a thick reddish purple #CC79A7 vertical divider with one large reddish purple dot drawn on it at the digit row, marking the decimal point (a drawn mark, not a text label).
Digit row, left to right: "2", "7", "5", "3", one digit per cell; 5 in teal #0072B2, 3 in amber #E69F00.
Exactly 4 columns; no Thousandths column, no extra rows, no fractions written.
rejection: the digits placed in the wrong columns, for example 5 under Hundredths
the decimal point divider placed anywhere other than between Ones and Tenths
the number written as anything other than 27.53
images.takeaway: In 27.53 the 5 counts tenths and the 3 counts hundredths.
images.description: A place value chart with columns Tens, Ones, Tenths and Hundredths holding the digits 2, 7, 5 and 3, with a dot marking the decimal point between Ones and Tenths, under the number 27.53.
images.context: Shown beside the recap text on tenths, hundredths and thousandths.
images.teaching_notes: Read each digit with its column name aloud: 2 tens, 7 ones, 5 tenths, 3 hundredths.

image_decisions.why: The place value chart is the clearest way to recall what each digit after the point is worth.
